design_note: 2005 centenary-era circular blue-and-gold ring, rampant staff lion, two roses and two balls; omits engraved names and dates.
Gold-framed crimson double-scroll motif, local merchant ship above the Red Devil and trident, gold balls on both sides; no text.
Liver bird and sprig on a white and red shield, Shankly Gates crown, twin memorial flames and the green lower ribbon. No lettering.
Contemporary 2002-origin taper shield, deep navy outer pinline, two distinct reds and an east-pointing gold cannon with wheel; no name.
2006 transition motif: tall navy cockerel with curved hackle, raised tail, and stitched old-style football. This is the 2006 refresh, not the earlier coat-of-arms layout.
Early-2000s roundel language: blue ring edged in old gold, stemmed red Lancashire rose on cream and a blank lower motto ribbon. Fresh drawn emblem.
1988-era Newcastle composition: twin silver hippocampi flank a black-and-white shield below a castle and cross pennant; blue ribbon without words.
Reebok-era blue orb and oversized asymmetric scarlet ribbon, before the 2013 rose return. Original football seam geometry replaces the historic initials.
1999 to Boleyn Ground farewell era: sky blue with claret crossed hammers under the castle. No modern London-only hammers badge.
Early-2000s civic crown and tree cue, newly drawn.
Lock-up tower, paired laurels and curved blue escutcheon; text omitted.
2001-era black and white tapered shield and red angular center. Three original red strokes evoke the period composition without spelling the club initials.
Red hand/arm and sword evoke Charlton’s historic primary motif; the outline remains distinctly pixelated and newly shaped.
1986–2007 circular Boro badge, scarlet outer ring and white field with a red rampant lion; no 2007 shield or dates.
1997 eagle, three stars and flat harbor shield, reworked in segmented pixel-ready shapes.
Aston Villa 2000–07 heritage: claret/sky vertical field, gilded lion and wine-colored cap; intentionally omits the star added on the next badge.
Approved P4 Harbour Trim. Same star and crescent. Softer crown and a double rim.
Globe-and-ball badge that Birmingham adopted in 1972, with distinctive blue ribbon and two stacked globes; freshly drawn with no inscriptions.
Blue/white stripes and bird on hawthorn kept as distinct heritage cues.
Sunderland 1997-era landmark shield: Penshaw Monument upper left, bridge lower right, dark flanking supporters and a red banner. Drawn without names or motto.
Blackpool’s civic seaside vocabulary presented with a new crenellated taper, recognizable tower and small water curls; no actual badge tracing.
Claret-and-amber Bradford heritage expressed with a new narrow shield, amber rails and side-on bantam; no 2005 badge details are duplicated.
Wing mark on the period-style blue/cream shield.
Civic quarter shield with bridge and robin cues.
Longstanding Burnley heraldic bird, cotton and chevron cues. Redrawn with a left-dropping wing and isolated river-chevron footline; 1996–97 period programme reference.
Bury’s arms use both anvil and bee. Here the bee spreads its wings above an isolated anvil rather than sitting above the city arms.
Coventry’s elephant carries a new stepped tower. Flanking wing triangles allude to Coventry’s civic supporters without replicating the official arms.
Palace’s longstanding eagle and exhibition-palace idea rendered as an asymmetric diving illustration with stepped glass dashes and no official silhouette or ribbon text.
Iconic Derby Ram cue from 1995–96 kit context, redrawn as a compressed profile with scored shoulder and high curled horn.
Grimsby Town Foundation documents the old striped field, fish icons and trawler. Established cue preserved with a redrawn hull, off-level fish and new silhouette.
Terrier, vertical sky-and-white and town-arm skyline adapted into a new castellated profile, preserving the dog cue without copying the exact shield.
Castle-gate outline, white Suffolk Punch and river details; movement and geometry redrawn.
Period white rose and yellow/navy are recognisable cues. Not a trace of either era’s badge; no crest frame or typography.
The official chronology dates wider lettering and borders to 2002–09. This mark echoes the bold blue roundel and fox/cinquefoil combination but removes names and retains a diagonal fox mask.
The 1995–96 programme shows the hat and balls at either side. This keeps those features separated as a pictogram, with no civic frame or text.
Lion crest documented in September 1995. The emphatic curling tail and blue-white body cite the historic animal without tracing its limb geometry or framing.
The original historical tree and water forms are readily identifiable. Asymmetrical silhouette and two displaced ripples differentiate it.
Notts heritage retains the visual black/white split and two magpies. Sloped field and hooked birds are new, so the recognizable idiom survives without redrawing the official device.
Heraldic Oldham owl/top and a football remain readable in an original ceramic-shaped crest, not a transplant of the source owl or later bare brand.
County ox crossing foreground water references the historic picture. Split pale horns and thick river glints emphasize the identity.
Classical lamb-and-cross flag is the source heraldic unit. New flag silhouette and squat animal stance, no lettering or crest frame.
QPR’s old monogram cannot be recreated without letters; instead blue-white hoops are the dominant period cue, with two badge-like accents.
Circular Reading crest direction with blue-white hoops, crown and a stylized red-field lion.
Crossed blades and Yorkshire rose put back in prominent steel and red/white, with angled guards and a three-tone rose set in a different arrangement.
The 1995–2016 civic owl concept carried into 2005–06. Rebuilds the narrow blue heraldic shape and gold crop detail, without lettering.
Halo, paneled football, scarf and green arboreal detail are reorganized into a compact halo-and-scarf silhouette.
Swindon wore the red/white/green diamond period badge in 2005–06. The abstract swap-lock device recalls its angular divisions without spelling the historical letter.
Black-edged gold pentagon and red Hertfordshire hart cue the long-running Watford era identity. Antlers and facial angle are completely redrawn.
Original Wimbledon concluded in 2004; bonus slot references the durable civic double-eagle identity instead of inventing a 2005/06 season.
Approved W3 Sable Cut. Same gold hexagon. New brow, eyes and muzzle.
Perched canary and ball with a reduced Norwich civic castle cue.
Uses the long-running bluebird with Welsh dragon and daffodil in the pre-2008 side of the Cardiff badge family. It is not a later red-primary redesign.
Familiar Stoke red-white stripe field with a pottery-era Stafford Knot accent. The heritage knot replaces rather than copies the exact period upper graphics.
Green shield, cream multi-sail Mayflower and unlettered lower scroll.
Tiger head returned in an escutcheon in 2001, reinforced by a local 2005 match programme. Custom muzzle and striping without title or date.

Uses the quartered 1994–2017 Brentford direction: beehive, civic blade strokes, red trim and white quadrants instead of the current standalone bee.
Original lamp emblem references Barnsley’s mining and civic traditions; no official coat of arms or period mark reproduced.
Swansea’s 1998 redesign replaced the castle-and-swan backing. Early-2000s swan association is now expressed as original sweeping ink curves and a single tide stroke.
Period-style club symbol; exact 1995 implementation not verified.
Industrial clenched-hand cue, composed from fresh finger and chain geometry.
Period-style club symbol; exact 1995 implementation not verified.
Black-white New Brompton split meets a Kent horse on blue. This is an original asymmetric profile/pose with the long-running period field hierarchy.
Yeovil’s coat-of-arms-related shirt crest was introduced in 1985. A distinct glove reflects the town’s glove-making nickname, not the civic mark.
Crooked church silhouette is the association, but twisted copperwork and stepped foreground are freshly constructed.
Bournemouth’s 1972-onward portrait and ball are remembered via a new motion-first anonymous player silhouette, not the official portrait or shield.
Tranmere-style civic towers and river in strong blue over a white-bordered shield.
Miller identity and old-town mill form interpreted as a new four-sail design. No official initials or background wordmark.
Hartlepool wore the ship-wheel badge introduced in 1995 in the requested period. An open helm with a new eight-spoke construction replaces the earlier hart, which was revived later.
Original letter-free interlocking metal strokes and a floating colored dot evoke the first MK Dons badge on its inaugural shirt. No MK initials, numerals, or official silhouette.
Original swift and football, drawing on Walsall Town Swifts and the bird motif rather than the framed kit crest.
Barnet-inspired amber and black bee with original faceted wing orientation.
Bristol Rovers’ documented 1997-onward pirate and blue-yellow badge, redrawn as a compact pirate bust and cutlass.
Cheltenham used civic arms before the 2010 robin redesign. Original paired spa-water birds and bath-wave symbol use the older civic direction, not the 2010 graphic.
Twin pale wyverns and a football read as Leyton Orient’s core symbols, but the shield and digitless mirrored geometry are new.
Period source club used a blue lion with wheat; this new crouching lion carries a silk spool, not its heraldic position or sheaf.
Lincoln’s imp-inspired marker in black on contrasting red and cream
Heraldic period direction from Northampton shirts; new single stone lion and symbolic cobbler’s leather, not the full civic arms.
Original lion/key shorthand based on civic arms vocabulary used for period Posh identity, without the actual arms layout.
Fictional original river cat built from broad Cheshire historic lion imagery. Not the Chester FC successor badge.
Original lion and two lock devices recall the original merged club’s heraldic lion and keys, not its combined crest or successor.
Rail motif tied to Darlington civic railway vocabulary; fictional locomotive, not the period Quakers badge.
Shrewsbury civic leopard-head cue on a circular blue-gold badge, with three separately simplified devices.
Original wool sack and two independent birds recall textile and martlet imagery visible in civic/1993 badge history.
Original civic center composition inside a round identity, not a hat-only nickname logo or Stockport’s real arms.
Mansfield’s 1994-era stag-head imagery inspires this running whole stag, without overlapping lettering or crest copy.
Original cupped-wing gull; historical badge motif family rather than a clipped or directly recolored Torquay mark.
Red Welsh dragon over a green-and-white field, intentionally one custom regional motif with no official banners or title.
Original Pilgrim trade ship silhouette, recalling the marine identity without reusing Boston’s crest or ring.
Club’s official navy/pale blue quarters and swan cue; new profile and unlettered geometry.
Fictional Border-club bonus crest; custom fox figure evokes Carlisle’s community fox motif without claiming it was the 2005 crest.
